title: Lesson 35: Domain Modeling: Entities, Aggregates, and Bounded Contexts Applied to Agent Design
description: The domain modeling discipline of entities, aggregates, bounded contexts, and ubiquitous language, and how it keeps a multi-agent system from collapsing into a tangle of overlapping prompts.

questions.question: A coverage rule says an incident on a lapsed policy is not covered, and it depends on policy status, coverage dates, and the incident date together. Where should the rule live?
options: In the agent's prompt, so the model can reason about the policy language.
Split across the tools that expose each field, so each one enforces its part.
In the output schema, which validates the shape of the model's response.
In the aggregate behind its root, decided together in one place.
questions.explanation: An aggregate is a consistency boundary: anything that must stay true together is read and decided behind the aggregate root, not assembled from separate sources in free text.

questions.question: A team is about to draw an agent graph for a new system. What should be established first?
options: The agent graph, because the available tools determine the responsibilities.
The bounded contexts and their shared language, since agents follow the model.
The prompt library, because the vocabulary inside each prompt defines the boundaries.
One all-purpose agent, split later only if its performance suffers.
questions.explanation: Agents are an implementation detail; the context map comes first, or the agent graph reproduces whatever tools happened to be available instead of the shape of the business.

questions.question: How should a domain system treat a state change proposed by a model?
options: As an authorized decision once the output schema accepts it as valid.
As a trusted instruction to execute immediately against stored state.
As an untrusted proposal the domain must authorize before executing.
As free text that a human reviewer must approve before any change is applied.
questions.explanation: A schema validates shape but cannot enforce meaning, so model output is an untrusted proposal that deterministic domain code must normalize, authorize, and then execute through the aggregate.
